summary: Priority fanout thrashing causing periodic 5xx spikes and connection oscillation for Composify Labs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Composify Labs - Dedicated) reported a pattern of elevated 5xx responses beginning 2026-03-13 18:10 UTC and recurring in ~10-15 minute clusters. Errors correlate with small-payload, very high QPS traffic routed with high-priority flags (priority-fanout). Impact: intermittent failures on production chat endpoint, elevated tail latency and stream disconnects.

Impact:
- Multiple customer calls failing with 5xx (502/503) for ~30% of requests during each wave.
- User-facing timeouts and aborted streaming sessions; Composify reported retries that compounded load.
- Business impact: degraded SLA for dedicated tenant, customer engineering actively blocked.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant pool in prod us-east (reserved GPU pool).
- API Gateway -> Ingress prioritizer -> routing layer -> serving-runtime pool (pinned model redwood/gpt-7b-ctx16k).
- Recent autoscaler/priority tweak deployed 2026-03-12 (optimize prefetch warmup).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Send many small, parallel chat requests with high-priority header (X-Rdwd-Priority: high) that fan out to multiple shards.
2) Observe short-lived bursts where API returns 502/503 for a subset of concurrent streams and non-streaming requests.
3) In the same period, runtime shows rapid connection churn and several worker restarts.
4) When traffic drops, system recovers; issue reappears on next burst.

Observed behavior:
- API Gateway logs show upstream reset/502s and 503s clustered to same routing buckets.
- Serving runtime logs report "KV cache contention" and "eviction thrash" followed by worker soft-restart (watchdog).
- Scheduler shows rapid prefetch invalidations and immediate refills for priority lanes.
- Autoscaler did not scale quickly enough due to short window and rapid oscillation.

Expected behavior:
- High-priority fanout should be handled without elevated 5xx floor; prefetch and KV cache should smooth warmups without causing thrash or worker restarts.

Logs & metrics (excerpts):
- apigw/us-east access: 2026-03-13T18:12:07Z 502 upstream-reset tenant=comp_lab shard=13
- runtime/shard-13: 2026-03-13T18:12:09Z "kvcache: lock_wait>150ms" "prefetch: invalidation=312"
- runtime/shard-13: 2026-03-13T18:12:10Z "watchdog: soft-restart triggered by memory-eviction-spike"
- autoscaler/events: 2026-03-13T18:12:15Z scale_up_attempt shard=13 reason=queue_growth but aborted due to cooldown

Additional context:
- Customer uses aggressive retry logic in their client (2 immediate retries) which amplified the waves.
- No platform-wide deploys during incident window except the autoscaler tweak on 03-12.
- Related historical tickets show similar patterns during priority reshuffles (linked issues).
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-13 18:15 UTC: Initial report from CS after customer call.
- 18:20 UTC: SRE reproduced burst locally with small-payload high-priority load.
- 18:30 UTC: Observed KV cache lock contention and immediate worker soft-restarts.
- 18:45 UTC: Applied temporary workaround (route high-priority fanout to a fallback route with larger prefetched KV cache).

Hypotheses considered:
1) Prefetch/kv cache invalidation loop for high-priority lanes is causing lock contention and eviction thrash, leading to runtime watchdog soft-restarts -> 5xx.
2) Autoscaler cooldown and rapid oscillation prevents timely scale-up for short bursts, causing queueing and upstream resets.
3) API gateway request fanout combined with client retry amplification is creating ephemeral connection storms that exhaust accept-queues.

Evidence:
- kvcache lock_wait metrics spike in exact time windows of 5xx.
- Worker restart logs reference high eviction churn.
- Autoscaler logs show aborted scale attempts during the wave.

Next steps (in progress):
- Engineering to instrument per-tenant kvcache lock histograms and add throttling on invalidation rate (assigned runtime-team).
- Temporarily route Composify high-priority traffic to fallback route with pre-warmed shards (mitigation applied at 18:45 UTC).
- Triage autoscaler cooldown policy for short-burst responsiveness; consider faster warmup for dedicated tenants.
- Ask Composify to reduce client-side immediate retries to prevent amplification during our mitigation window.
- Create a canary test to simulate small-payload high-priority fanout to validate fix.
comments: 2026-03-13 18:21 - CS (Morgan L.): Customer reported 502/503 spikes starting ~18:10 UTC. They noted retries made things worse. Requested urgent assistance.
2026-03-13 18:25 - SRE (Jayden K. Patel): Reproduced with a synthetic client. Observed kvcache lock wait >150ms and runtime soft-restart. Routing to runtime shard 13 shows repeated invalidations.
2026-03-13 18:30 - Eng (Priya S.): Hypothesis: prefetch invalidation loop for priority lanes. Will add tracing to prefetch path and rate-limit invalidations. ETA 4 hours for first patch.

2026-03-13 18:45 - Ops (Jayden K. Patel): Temporary mitigation applied: rerouted Composify high-priority traffic to pre-warmed fallback route. Customer still seeing reduced errors; monitoring closely.
2026-03-13 19:05 - CS (Morgan L.): Composify confirms error rate dropped from ~30% to ~4% during last wave after mitigation. They ask for permanent mitigation plan and timeline.

2026-03-14 09:10 - Runtime Team Lead (Priya S.): Added instrumentation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5042 to rate-limit invalidation bursts and expose per-tenant lock metrics. Requesting review.
2026-03-14 12:00 - SRE (Jayden K. Patel): Autoscaler cooldown removed for dedicated pre-warm policy in us-east; monitoring for oscillation. Will coordinate rollout with infra.
resolution: Workaround applied: high-priority traffic for Composify routed to pre-warmed fallback pool at 2026-03-13 18:45 UTC reducing error rate. Full fix in progress: runtime PR to add invalidation rate-limiter and per-tenant kvcache tracing (PR opened). Autoscaler prewarm policy adjustment proposed and partially rolled out for dedicated tenants in us-east. Postmortem and permanent remediation plan scheduled after verification.
